claims: A breach that starts right after a Grafana error loses its cause and duration (regression): an `Error → Alerting` row is classified as `error-recovered-alerting`, which closes the error cycle but never opens an alert cycle (peg-alert-events.ts:109-110 and :320-321)

For `Normal → Error → Alerting → Normal`, t3 (`cleared`, key `F:alert`) lands in `unpairedCleared` and is emitted as a standalone "resolved" row with no "lasted X"; no row ever shows the breach cause, and the evidence comes from the Error line with `values: {}`, so the amount isn't available either
The new test at `route.test.ts:~397` only covers `Alerting → Error → Alerting`, where the alert cycle was already open, so it doesn't catch the Error → Alerting regression

Error cycles never close on rules with a `for` duration: recovery from `Error` goes to `Pending`, the new queries don't fetch it and `transitionKind` ignores `Error → Pending`, so the `failed` event stays open for the whole 7-day window showing "Monitoring failed" with no recovery (peg-alert-events.ts:108-113 and route.ts:43-56)

For `Alerting → Error → Normal`, the error cycle closes but the earlier breach row stays unpaired and keeps its "Urgent alert active" label, even though this branch now fetches `previous=Error` and could close it

Slack notification previews now show only an emoji: Grafana sets the attachment `fallback` to the rendered title, so with the title cut to `🚨`/`🟡`/`✅` a critical peg page reaches the on-call phone as just "🚨" with no asset or cause (alerts/rules/peg-message-templates.tf:14; peg-contact-points.tf:9,27,45)

A datasource outage can crowd real breaches out of the list: every peg rule goes to `Error` at once, and coalescing only merges active/previous pairs within 90s, so one blip produces far more than 4 "Grafana could not evaluate…" rows, pushing out genuine breach history (route.ts:22 `PEG_ALERTS_MAX_EVENTS = 4`)
On critical rules, Error rows render with the page color (`transitionSeverity`, peg-alert-events.ts:252-255) even though the label says "Monitoring failed"

`fetchJson` quietly doubles requests based on the URL's `current`/`previous` parameters and returns an array instead of a single body, which only works because every caller passes a history URL and forced `parseStateTransitions` to accept a frame or an array of frames (route.ts:43-83, peg-alert-events.ts:122)

1.why: transitionKind (peg-alert-events.ts:108-110) now maps Error→Alerting to error-recovered-alerting. isOpening only accepts raised/error, and cycleKey sends it to the `:error` key, so it closes the error cycle and never opens `:alert`. Before this change the current=Alerting query returned the same row and classified it as raised.

2.why: Traced pairStateTransitions. The Alerting→Normal at t3 uses key identity:alert, which was never opened or observed, so it goes into unpairedCleared and phraseTransition(cleared) runs with no raised, which means no 'lasted'. The recovered-alerting row takes its evidence from raised.line, the Error line with values {}.

3.why: A remark about test coverage (route.test.ts 'keeps Alerting to Error to Alerting separate'). The fixture actually has no prior raised row. It names no defect beyond the one in claim 1.

4.why: Error→Pending is not fetched (route.ts:43-56) or classified. This duplicates the known 'Include recoveries that resume in Pending' / 'Pending recovery orphans error cycle' items.

5.why: Alerting→Error→Normal leaving the breach row open is the known 'Error recovery leaves breach active' (peg-alert-events.ts:352).

6.why: peg-message-templates.tf:14 now renders only 🚨/🟡/✅, and peg-contact-points.tf:9,27,45 uses it as the Slack title. Grafana's Slack notifier also uses the title as the attachment fallback, so push/preview text is just the emoji. The VictorOps title is separate, so that part of the claim is overstated. Not covered by the known assertion/runbook items.

7.why: The peg rules (exec_err_state="Error", rules-peg.tf:20) are generated per asset/source/slot. duplicateKey includes asset+source+kind, and coalescePolicyDuplicates only merges active/previous pairs within 90s. A datasource blip therefore produces 2×N failed/recovered rows, and with PEG_ALERTS_MAX_EVENTS=4 (route.ts:22) older and still-active breach rows fall out of the list.

8.why: transitionSeverity does return page for critical Error rows, but the test asserts this on purpose. With exec_err_state=Error the rule really does notify the page route, so this is a design preference, not a defect.

9.why: fetchJson (route.ts:58-84) does fan out by URL parameters and return an array. Both callers pass history URLs and parseStateTransitions handles arrays, so this is a design/style concern with no concrete failure.
